To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the increase in PEF from baseline can be used to evaluate the effect of bronchodilator therapy in asthma, and that the best categorization of the increase in PEF was into five grades using Akaike information criterion (AIC) and that improvement scores can be used to assess the global improvement rating (GR).

the best categorization was determined using AIC and that increase in morning and evening peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) or mean PEFR was practicably used as an evaluation index for global improvement rating.
the morning PEFR is the most useful index for assessing global improvement, and the increase in PEPF from baseline is a practical evaluation index for global improvement in asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a tentative index for evaluating the efficacy of bronchial asthma treatment, the improvement score, and the results suggest the possibility of its use as an objective index.
the development of a new method for the evaluation of asthma treatment.
the development of a new method for the evaluation of asthma therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increase in PEFR was useful as a parameter of evaluation for GIR, and the improvement score was a useful index for assessment of improvement in asthma patients.

the morning and evening PEFs are both suitable as a measure for the assessment of asthma control, and that the best categorization of morning and evening PEF increases is > or = 5, 5-> or = 3, 3-> or = 1, 1-> or = -1 and < -1 for morning PEFR, mean PEFR and increase in evening PEF, respectively.
the increase from baseline of PEFR in morning and evening is an effective index for the assessment of GIR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increase from baseline PEFRs were practicable as an objective evaluation index in asthma and that a scoring system based on the increase in PEF would be a useful index for the evaluation of asthma.
PEFRs are useful as a surrogate marker for GIR, and that the best categorization of PEFRs for GIR is > or = 10% increase in PEFR for morning and mean PEFRs and > or =15% increase for evening PEFRs.
increase from baseline of PEFRs is a useful index for the evaluation of asthma improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the improvement score as a quantitative evaluation index in clinical trials of asthma treatment.
the improvement scores are useful in the assessment of global improvement in asthma patients.
a simple and practical evaluation of asthma control is possible by using PEFRs.
